2607.24300.title: Self-Authored Verification Is Unreliable in Heuristic Self-Improving Agents
2607.24300.paper_summary: Self-improving agents accumulate capability by repeatedly rewriting procedural policies, controllers, or heuristic rules. They typically rely on self-authored tests or metrics to decide whether to accept subsequent edits. The agent controls both the optimized object and its verifier. As a result, self-assigned scores can remain near perfect while real deployment performance degrades or stays low. We study this problem through the verifier--deployment gap. This gap refers to the discrepancy between an agent's self-authored verification signal and a sealed deployment evaluation that the agent cannot observe or access. We ask how self-authored verification fails under iterative policy-and-test rewriting, how the failure changes with capability, and how little exogenous trust is sufficient to prevent real regressions from being deployed. To address this problem, we introduce a Sealed Exogenous Acceptance Loop (SEAL). SEAL retains self-authored tests but compares each candidate with the incumbent through a fixed harness-side audit. The agent cannot author or inspect the audit, receives only accept/reject, and the whole incumbent state is retained after a clear regression. Our experiments show that this problem often appears in heuristic learning settings. These settings require trial-and-error discovery of the target objective. We further find that failures of self-written verification are stratified by capability. Weaker agents tend to damage previously acquired strategies behind easy self-tests. Stronger agents are more stable, but they still mismeasure the deployment distribution. Standard self-written constraints do not reliably close this gap. In contrast, SEAL outperforms unprotected baselines across six models and three random seeds. Reliable self-improvement need not abandon self-verification, but it requires at least one deployment-acceptance signal outside the agent's control.
2607.24300.paper_summary_zh: 自我提升的代理透過反覆重寫程序政策、控制器或啟發式規則來累積能力。它們通常依賴自我撰寫的測試或指標來決定是否接受後續的編輯。該代理同時控制優化對象及其驗證者。因此，自評分數可以保持接近完美，而實際部署性能卻下降或保持低水平。我們通過驗證者與部署之間的差距來研究這個問題。這個差距指的是代理自我撰寫的驗證信號與一個代理無法觀察或訪問的封閉部署評估之間的差異。我們詢問在迭代政策和測試重寫下，自我撰寫的驗證如何失敗，這種失敗如何隨著能力的變化而變化，以及需要多少外部信任才能防止實際回退被部署。為了解決這個問題，我們引入了一個封閉的外部接受循環（SEAL）。SEAL 保留自我撰寫的測試，但通過固定的審計來比較每個候選者與現任者。代理無法撰寫或檢查審計，只能接收接受/拒絕的結果，並且在明確的回退後保留整個現任狀態。我們的實驗顯示，這個問題在啟發式學習環境中經常出現。這些環境需要通過試錯來發現目標對象。我們進一步發現，自我撰寫驗證的失敗是根據能力分層的。較弱的代理往往在簡單的自我測試中損害之前獲得的策略。較強的代理則更穩定，但它們仍然錯誤地測量部署分佈。標準的自我撰寫約束無法可靠地縮小這一差距。相比之下，SEAL 在六個模型和三個隨機種子上表現優於未受保護的基線。可靠的自我提升不必放棄自我驗證，但至少需要一個在代理控制之外的部署接受信號。
